+  gkyl_position_map_slope(gpm, ix_map, x, dx, lower, upper);
+  ```
+
+  Here `x` is the computational coordinate, `dx` is the maximum finite-difference
+  step, and the bounds belong to the selected map in the full three-dimensional
+  geometry coordinates. This also handles 1D/2D simulations whose geometry is
+  constructed in three dimensions. Rank boundaries no longer determine the
+  derivative stencil. The header documents the accuracy and boundary policy.
+- **Store backup derivatives for X-point compression.**
+  `gkyl_position_map_xpt_ctx` gains `map_derivs_backup[3]`, alongside its saved
+  maps and contexts. A null backup derivative requests numerical differentiation.
+  Restoring a user map can therefore restore its matching derivative as well.
+
+**Compatibility:** all repository callers were updated. External callers must
+change their last two arguments, and code using the changed context structure
+must be rebuilt.
+
+## 2. Position-map construction, derivatives, and storage
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/position_map.c](gyrokinetic/zero/position_map.c).
+
+### Initialization and map selection
+
+- Both the ordinary and null constructors zero-initialize the map and its
+  constant-B, X-point, and magnetic-field contexts with `gkyl_calloc`. Unset
+  fields start from defined values.
+- Identity derivative backups are initialized in all three directions.
+- User-input map cases share one initialization block, and polynomial/numeric
+  constant-dB cases share another. Explicit `break` statements prevent
+  accidental fallthrough into unrelated map-type initialization.
+- X-point setup saves all three user maps, contexts, and derivatives. The old
+  loop saved only the first two maps and did not save derivatives.
+- `gkyl_position_map_set_compression` restores the derivative together with
+  each restored map/context, including the angular direction. Disabling
+  compression no longer leaves a compression derivative attached to a user map.
+
+### Numerical derivative policy
+
+- An available analytic derivative is called at the supplied computational
+  coordinate. If analytic derivatives are enabled but a direction has no
+  derivative callback, that direction falls back to finite differences.
+- The numerical path asserts a positive step and ordered bounds, accepts a
+  roundoff-sized coordinate overshoot, and clamps that overshoot to the domain.
+- It uses `(M(x+h)-M(x-h))/(2h)` when both samples are inside the global domain.
+- Near a global endpoint, it selects the inward direction and uses the
+  second-order three-point formula. The step is reduced when needed so both
+  displaced samples remain inside the domain.
+- Only the selected stencil points are evaluated. The old routine evaluated
+  points on both sides before deciding which stencil to use, so even a
+  discarded point could call a map outside its supported domain.
+
+These changes give both copies of an internal MPI face the same derivative
+and preserve second-order accuracy at physical endpoints.
+
+### Automatic-map storage and reference flux
+
+- Repeated `gkyl_position_map_set_bmag` calls free the previous extrema positions,
+  field values, and minimum/maximum flags before replacing them.
+- Extrema arrays have capacity `2*N_theta_boundaries + 1`, matching the sample
+  count used by the extrema search instead of the previous smaller allocation.
+- Numeric constant-dB optimization samples the arithmetic radial midpoint,
+  `(psi_min+psi_max)/2`. The previous square-root midpoint was undefined for
+  negative tokamak flux labels. This also changes the reference surface for
+  positive intervals; it is a deliberate change to the sampling convention.
+
+## 3. Automatic constant-dB maps and compression formulas
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_position_map_priv.h](gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_position_map_priv.h).
+
+### Extrema and degenerate fields
+
+- Equal or otherwise unclassified extrema receive a defined minimum/maximum
+  flag. Previously, these branches printed an error but left the flag unset.
+- Numeric mapping returns the identity exactly when `map_strength` is zero.
+- A field with negligible total variation, measured relative to its magnitude
+  using `DBL_EPSILON`, also returns the identity. A constant field supplies no
+  variation from which to construct a constant-dB redistribution.
+- `<float.h>` supplies the roundoff scale for these decisions.
+
+### Root finding and partial strength
+
+- Endpoint-root branches now join the common mapping-result path. They apply
+  strength blending and slope limits just like roots found inside an interval.
+  Previously, early returns skipped those operations and could introduce jumps.
+- The principal endpoint-root test uses `16*DBL_EPSILON*bscale` in place of a
+  fixed absolute `1e-10` threshold, making it relative to the field magnitude.
+- The Ridders solve allows 100 iterations instead of 10 and uses tolerance
+  `1e-12` instead of `1e-6`. This reduces root-position error before geometry
+  differentiates the resulting map. Difficult maps may take longer to initialize.
+
+### Slope-limit anchors
+
+An extremum's physical coordinate generally differs from its computational
+preimage under a constant-dB map. The old limiter assumed they were equal.
+
+The limiter now finds each endpoint's computational location from the cumulative
+magnetic-field variation, blends its physical location with the identity
+according to `map_strength`, and anchors the limiting line as
+`Theta_endpoint + slope*(theta-theta_endpoint)`. It also uses the computational
+midpoint to select the appropriate side. This removes the discontinuity exposed
+by an asymmetric-field test when root finding moves between regions.
+
+### X-point and separatrix compression
+
+- The sinusoidal maps and derivatives are algebraically simplified to avoid
+  the intermediate factor `1/(1-compression_factor)`. Compression factor 1
+  now gives a finite identity map and unit derivative.
+- The radial map and its derivative use `radial_compression_factor`. They
+  previously used the parallel `compression_factor`, so the two controls were
+  not independent.
+
+## 4. Shared construction of geometry-node coordinates
+
+New file:
+[gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_gk_geometry_node_coords_priv.h](gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_gk_geometry_node_coords_priv.h).
+
+The private `gk_geometry_node_coord` helper first forms an integer global node
+index from the local cell offset and local nodal index. It then evaluates either
+a Gauss node inside a cell or an equally spaced corner/face node. Exact global
+endpoints return the stored grid bounds directly.
+
+This replaces floating-point accumulation from a rank-local origin. A shared
+node therefore follows the same arithmetic on either rank. The helper accepts
+the number of Gauss nodes or intervals per cell rather than hard-coding the P1
+alternating increments. Mirror, mapc2p, and tokamak constructors include it.
+
+## 5. Mirror geometry
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c](gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c).
+
+### One implementation for every node layout
+
+The corner, interior, and surface constructors now delegate to `mggen_new`.
+Its layout parameter distinguishes corners, volume quadrature, and the three
+surface orientations. It derives node counts from the local cell and nodal
+ranges, selects Gauss or face coordinates by direction, and shares the
+equilibrium interpolation, radial root solve, allocation, and cleanup logic.
+
+This removes the three large copies of the same geometry formulas and the
+local `calc_running_coord` accumulator. Future changes to chain rules and
+boundary handling have one implementation to update.
+
+### Computational coordinates and chain rules
+
+- The axial computational coordinate `zcomp` is retained separately from
+  `Z = M(zcomp)`. `gkyl_position_map_slope` receives `zcomp` and global bounds.
+  The nominal numerical step is one computational cell.
+- Radial and angular position maps are applied as well as the axial map.
+  Their slopes enter the tangent vectors, dual vectors, and Jacobian.
+- On a constant-psi field line, define `q = -psi_Z/psi_R` and `D = dZ/dz`.
+  The axial tangent changes from `(q, 0, D)` to `(q*D, 0, D)`. It now satisfies
+  `e_3 dot grad(psi) = 0` and is reciprocal to the corresponding dual basis.
+- With `P = dpsi/dx` and `A = dphi/dalpha`, the off-axis Jacobian includes
+  all mapping factors: `J = (R/psi_R)*P*A*D`. For sqrt-psi coordinates,
+  `P` includes the additional `2*sqrt(psi)` factor. Downstream metrics and
+  the normal magnetic-field projection are regenerated from this geometry.
+
+### Sqrt-psi coordinates and the axis
+
+- The global radial grid is converted to sqrt-psi coordinates before local
+  offsets are applied. Radial decomposition therefore samples the same global
+  coordinates as a full-domain construction.
+- Only the true global lower radial corner/face can be treated as the axis.
+  An internal rank boundary is not an axis.
+- `nodes_psi` is explicitly assigned at every node, including zero on the axis.
+- Each geometry structure is zero-initialized before its components are filled.
+  Axis formulas retain the existing singular-basis convention and asymptotic
+  Jacobian, with the applicable mapping factors included.
+
+### Curl of the unit magnetic field
+
+The mirror curl calculation now uses the same field orientation as the rest of
+the mirror geometry: `B_R = -psi_Z/R`, `B_Z = psi_R/R`. Derivatives include
+the derivatives of `1/R`, and the normalization terms use the correct signs
+and `1/B^2` factors. The returned angular component retains its contravariant
+cylindrical-coordinate convention. These corrections also matter for uniform
+position maps; they were found during the nonuniform-grid audit.
+
+## 6. Generic mapc2p geometry
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/gk_geometry_mapc2p.c](gyrokinetic/zero/gk_geometry_mapc2p.c).
+
+- Corner, interior, and surface coordinates use the shared global-index helper
+  in every configuration direction.
+- Interior and tangential surface nodes use the Gauss ordinate table; the
+  surface-normal direction uses cell faces. Rank-local origins, alternating
+  increments, and the old ad hoc polynomial-order spacing factor are removed.
+- Map callbacks receive separate input and output variables. The old calls
+  reused the same address for both, which is incompatible with callbacks that
+  declare restricted input/output pointers.
+- Finite-difference displacements are applied in computational coordinates
+  before mapping. Their scale is `0.01*grid.dx` without the removed spacing
+  multiplier; this preserves the P1 scale used in validation.
+- Obsolete coordinate variables and minor spacing are cleaned up. The existing
+  global-boundary selection of mapc2p's surface stencils is retained.
+
+## 7. Cartesian magnetic-field projection
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/calc_metric.c](gyrokinetic/zero/calc_metric.c).
+
+`gkyl_calc_metric_advance_bcart` evaluates its input arrays at interior Gauss
+nodes. Its final nodal-to-modal conversion now also specifies interior Gauss
+nodes (`true`). It previously specified corner nodes (`false`), which selected
+the wrong samples and made the Cartesian unit-field output depend on the local
+MPI range. A comment records the matching input/output convention.
+
+The varying-direction mapc2p regression detects this error; a constant Cartesian
+field can conceal it. The one-versus-six-rank Boltzmann mirror comparison changed
+from about 24.7% maximum-norm disagreement to exact agreement for this output.
+
+## 8. Tokamak geometry
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/tok_geo.c](gyrokinetic/zero/tok_geo.c).
+
+- Corner, volume, and surface nodes use the global-index coordinate helper,
+  including donor/recipient angular coordinates used for axisymmetric copies.
+- Computational theta is formed directly from the grid before mapping. The
+  old conversion through accumulated arc length and back to theta is removed;
+  mapped theta is still converted to arc length for the equilibrium solve.
+- The erroneous spacing expression
+  `poly_order == 1.0/poly_order` is removed. That expression was a Boolean
+  comparison and became zero for P2; node placement now uses explicit counts.
+- Radial and parallel slope calls use computational coordinates and global
+  bounds under the new API. Corner radial mapping uses separate input/output
+  storage.
+- Replicated angular planes apply the radial position map before evaluating
+  the equilibrium-dependent curl, including displaced radial stencil points.
+  Previously those evaluations used the unmapped flux label.
+- The interior safety-factor profile is copied from the donor plane to each
+  other angular plane, avoiding uninitialized replica entries.
+- Expensive corner geometry is calculated on one donor angular plane. The
+  previous loop calculated a second plane that the replication loop overwrote.
+- Curl derivatives include the radial derivatives of the `1/R` factors and
+  the missing `1/R` in the toroidal contribution to `dB/dZ`. All three components
+  use the corrected magnetic-field normalization terms. The tokamak field-sign
+  convention is preserved.
+- Superseded arc-length increments, local origins, and related spacing are
+  removed with the coordinate-construction changes.
+
+## 9. EFIT data with a vanishing toroidal field function
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/zero/efit.c](gyrokinetic/zero/efit.c).
+
+The reader stores the tabulated `F*F'` values first and computes `F'` in a common
+loop after either flux-order reading branch. Where `F` is nonzero, it divides
+by `F` as before. Where `F` is zero, it differentiates the tabulated `F` using
+neighboring values: centered differences inside the table and one-sided
+differences at its endpoints.
+
+This prevents `0/0` values from entering the geometry of the purely poloidal
+straight-cylinder fixture used in the tokamak tests.
+
+## 10. MPI stability estimate
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/apps/gyrokinetic.c](gyrokinetic/apps/gyrokinetic.c).
+
+`gkyl_gyrokinetic_app_omegaH_init` now performs an MPI maximum reduction of the
+geometry factor after its local reduction and normalization. The density and
+geometry maxima can occur on different ranks; combining only local maxima
+previously weakened the omega-H timestep constraint when the decomposition
+separated them. A shared geometry maximum restores the full-domain bound.
+
+This adds one host-side collective during initialization. In the WHAM check,
+the previously different timestep histories on six/eight ranks now match the
+one-rank history exactly.
+
+## 11. Physical wall-flux diagnostics
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/apps/gk_species_bflux.c](gyrokinetic/apps/gk_species_bflux.c).
+
+Both the instantaneous volume-integrated and cumulative volume/time-integrated
+charged-species boundary diagnostics test whether the local domain owns the
+requested global boundary. Integration uses factor 1 for that physical boundary
+and factor 0 for an internal MPI boundary before the plane reduction.
+
+In 1D the plane communicator includes every spatial rank. Previously, nonzero
+initial fluxes at internal boundaries entered the wall diagnostic. Restricting
+its contribution restores the physical-wall total and allows the particle
+budget to be checked consistently across decompositions.
+
+## 12. Regression input configuration supplied for the investigation
+
+These position-map input changes were already present when implementation
+started and are included in the working diff:
+
+| File | Geometry | Mapping addition |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| [rt_gk_wham_1x2v_p1.c](gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_wham_1x2v_p1.c) | Mirror | Numeric constant-dB map, strength 1.0 |
+| [rt_gk_mirror_boltz_elc_1x2v_p1.c](gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_mirror_boltz_elc_1x2v_p1.c) | mapc2p mirror | Numeric constant-dB map, strength 0.5 |
+
+Both specify maximum slopes of 2 at field minima and maxima, Gaussian standard
+deviation 0.5, and maximum integration width 1.0. The Boltzmann input also adds
+the comma needed before its new `position_map_info` member.
+
+**Resolution versus validation:** the current source defaults are 32 axial
+cells for WHAM and 16 for the Boltzmann mirror. Resolution changes are absent
+from the current diff. The recorded MPI validation used 192 axial cells. To
+select that resolution with the current WHAM input, use `-x 192`, for example:
+
+```sh
+mpirun -n 6 ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_wham_1x2v_p1 -M -c 6 -x 192 -s1
+```
+
+Use an MPI launcher matching the MPI library linked into the executable.
+
+## 13. Position-map unit tests
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_position_map.c](gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_position_map.c).
+
+Existing derivative calls are updated to the new bounds-based API. Three test
+entries are added, bringing this executable to 17 cases:
+
+| Added case | What it verifies |
+| --- | --- |
+| `slope_global_bounds` | All three map indices on 1D/2D/3D simulation grids; endpoints and nearby/interior points; steps larger than the domain; no out-of-domain callbacks; factor-of-four error reduction when halving the step for a cubic; analytic derivatives bypass map evaluation. |
+| `compression_parameters` | Independent radial/parallel factors; radial map values; finite identity maps and unit slopes at factor 1; restoration of a saved user map with numerical derivative fallback when compression is disabled. |
+| `numeric_degenerate_and_strength` | Constant and asymmetric fields; negative flux labels; strengths 0, 0.5, and 1; exact extremum preimages; continuity, monotonicity, and slope limits; repeated magnetic-field setup and cleanup. |
+
+Small bounded polynomial callbacks count evaluations and detect unsupported
+sample coordinates. An asymmetric piecewise-linear field exposes errors hidden
+by symmetric extrema.
+
+## 14. Geometry regression tests
+
+New file:
+[gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_geometry_nonuniform.c](gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_geometry_nonuniform.c).
+
+The test has its own node-coordinate calculation and analytic map derivatives.
+It constructs full and partitioned geometries sequentially, so its partition
+checks run without an MPI launcher. Actual MPI evolution is checked separately.
+
+Seven mirror cases use the exactly representable equilibrium
+`psi(R,Z) = R^2*(1+Z^2)/2`:
+
+| Case | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `mirror_identity` | Baseline identity mapping. |
+| `mirror_affine` | Nonunit analytic slope; isolates tangent chain-rule errors. |
+| `mirror_nonlinear_numeric` | Computational-coordinate and numerical-stencil correctness. |
+| `mirror_nonlinear_analytic` | Nonlinear mapping with supplied derivatives. |
+| `mirror_sqrt_psi` | Sqrt-psi radial convention with a nonlinear axial map. |
+| `mirror_all_maps` | Nonlinear radial, angular, and axial maps together in psi coordinates. |
+| `mirror_nonuniform_axis` | Sqrt-psi geometry including the axis with a nonlinear axial map. |
+
+They cover corners, interior nodes, all surface orientations, and partitions
+in each configuration direction. Assertions check mapping slopes, analytic
+Jacobians, reciprocal bases away from the singular axis, normal magnetic-field
+projection, curl, and partition agreement of the Jacobian.
+
+Three further cases complete the executable's 10 cases:
+
+- `mapc2p_partitions` uses a curved Cartesian map with a varying-direction,
+  divergence-free magnetic field. It detects the Cartesian-field projection
+  error that a constant field would hide.
+- `tokamak_partitions_numeric` and `tokamak_partitions_analytic` use the
+  checked-in straight-cylinder equilibrium with radial and parallel maps.
+- These cases compare corner positions/maps, interior/surface Jacobians,
+  metrics, tangent and dual vectors, magnetic fields, curls, normal projections,
+  surface lengths, and modal Cartesian unit-field arrays. Independent checks
+  cover the axial tangent and analytic curl.
+- Comparisons include 2, 4, and 8 partitions where the mesh permits. Floating
+  values are checked for finiteness using their exponent bits, so the check
+  remains effective in the build's `-ffast-math` configuration.
+
+## 15. Existing mapc2p test fixture
+
+File: [gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gk_geometry_mapc2p.c](gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gk_geometry_mapc2p.c).
+
+The nonlinear axial fixture is blended equally with the identity map, and
+`dmapz_dz` is changed to its matching derivative. The old fixture had zero
+slope at its lower endpoint and therefore a singular Jacobian. The new
+lower-endpoint slope is 0.5; the test still exercises a nonlinear map while
+avoiding that unintended degeneracy.
+
+## 16. MPI output checker
+
+New file:
+[gyrokinetic/creg/check_nonuniform_mpi.py](gyrokinetic/creg/check_nonuniform_mpi.py).
+
+This NumPy/postgkyl script compares saved short WHAM evolutions in directories
+named `RUNS-N` against a one-rank reference. The output prefix and rank list
+are configurable; the default ranks are 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8. It reports results
+as JSON and fails assertions on inconsistent results.
+
+It checks:
+
+- Compatible array shapes, finite values, timestep histories, corner/interior
+  geometry arrays, and initial/final ion, electron, and field snapshots.
+- Both copies of shared scalar faces for `jacobgeo`, `B3`, `bmag`, and `lenr`,
+  along with the lower-face values and the global upper face. It accounts for
+  the special output layout: component 1 holds an upper-face value only at
+  each rank's last cell.
+- Particle-count histories, physical-wall flux histories, and the steady
+  source assumption required by this particular fixture.
+- The particle budget using each step's RK-weighted wall-flux diagnostic
+  directly. It reports the residual relative to both the initial count and
+  the net particle change.
+
+The comparisons use explicit tolerances; bitwise equality is an observed
+result of the recorded runs, not a universal requirement imposed by the script.
+
+## 17. Validation record and measured results
+
+New file:
+[gyrokinetic/creg/nonuniform_validation.md](gyrokinetic/creg/nonuniform_validation.md).
+
+The validation record documents the original reproduction, build/MPI setup,
+before/after measurements, unit tests, Valgrind scope, short-evolution settings,
+particle-budget calculation, and coverage limits. [BUG_REPORT.md](BUG_REPORT.md)
+is the supplied investigation report and was not rewritten as part of the fix.
+
+The completed checks recorded there are:
+
+| Check | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Six-rank WHAM maximum shared-face Jacobian mismatch | 8.52038951% before; 0 after. |
+| Six-rank WHAM maximum shared-face B3 mismatch | 0.65592459% before; 0 after. |
+| Six-rank WHAM maximum streaming-factor mismatch | 7.85500051% before; 0 after. |
+| Unit tests | 53 passed: 10 geometry-nonuniform, 17 position-map, 8 mirror-grid, 2 mirror-geometry, 2 mapc2p-geometry, 4 tokamak-geometry, and 10 EFIT cases. |
+| Short WHAM evolution on 1/2/4/6/8 ranks | 21 steps each, no RK-stage failures; identical saved distributions, fields, compared geometry, and timestep histories. |
+| Particle budget | Maximum residual below 2e-15 of the initial particle count. |
+| Boltzmann mapc2p mirror on 1/6 ranks | Successful one-step runs; identical compared corner/interior geometry and shared scalar faces. |
+| Focused Valgrind runs | Zero errors and zero bytes in use at exit for position-map and geometry cases. |
+
+The geometry Valgrind run used a smaller mapc2p/tokamak mesh and a maximum of
+two partitions; the ordinary numerical geometry tests used their full test
+meshes and up to eight partitions. Detailed commands and temporary artifact
+locations are in the validation record.
+
+## 18. Interpretation and remaining limits
+
+- The changed derivative API and context layout require rebuilding dependent
+  code. Corrected geometry and automatic maps can change serial results as
+  well as MPI results; these repairs address physical-coordinate errors in
+  addition to shared-face disagreement.
+- GPU execution was unavailable, so CPU/GPU agreement has not been established.
+  The completed evolutions are short P1 tests, not a long production rerun or
+  an exhaustive convergence study of every map, equilibrium, or block layout.

+  supported axisymmetric convention. The tokamak cases exercise radial and
+  parallel remapping.
+- The existing surface-CFL estimator additionally considers each MPI
+  subdomain's upper face. Some per-cell CFL diagnostic values therefore remain
+  decomposition-dependent. Its global maximum and the final timestep/solution
+  histories agreed in the recorded WHAM check; that estimator was not changed.
+- The test results establish the fixes within the exercised configurations.
+  They do not prove universal absence of nonuniform-grid bugs.
*** End Patch"));
